title: Go: Plugin Architecture
description: Design a flexible plugin system using Go interfaces, a registry pattern, and plugin composition.

steps.title: Define the plugin interface
steps.description: Define a `Plugin` interface with methods `Name() string`, `Init() error`, and `Execute(data map[string]interface{}) (interface{}, error)`. Then create a `BasePlugin` struct embedding the basics. Print the interface definition with `fmt.Println`.
hints: Interfaces are satisfied implicitly in Go
Define the interface in a clean block
BasePlugin can embed a name field

verification.failureMessage: Print the Plugin interface definition to output.

steps.title: Implement the registry pattern
steps.description: Create a `Registry` struct with a `sync.RWMutex` and a `map[string]Plugin`. Implement `Register(p Plugin) error` (returns error if name exists), `Get(name string) (Plugin, bool)`, and `List() []string`. Print registered plugin names after registering two plugins.
hints: Use RWMutex for safe concurrent access
Register should check for duplicate names
List should return sorted keys for deterministic output

verification.failureMessage: Print the list of registered plugin names.

steps.title: Load plugins from a map
steps.description: Create a function `LoadPlugins(plugins map[string]Plugin, reg *Registry) []error` that registers all plugins from the map, collecting any errors. Print which plugins loaded successfully and which failed using `fmt.Printf`.
hints: Map iteration order is random; sort keys for deterministic output
Use ok pattern to check registration results

steps.title: Plugin with configuration
steps.description: Create a `ConfigurablePlugin` struct that embeds `BasePlugin` and adds a `Config map[string]string` field. Implement a `Configure(key, value string)` method and make `Execute` use the config. Demonstrate by configuring and executing.
hints: Embed BasePlugin to reuse name and Init
Store config as a simple map
Execute should print which config keys it's using

steps.title: Compose multiple plugins
steps.description: Create a `Pipeline` struct that implements `Plugin` and holds a slice of `Plugin`. Its `Execute` method runs each sub-plugin in sequence, passing the output data of one as input to the next. Print the pipeline execution trace using `fmt.Println`.
hints: Pipeline implements Plugin by running children sequentially
Pass data between plugins through the map parameter
Print each step with pipeline step index

verification.failureMessage: Print each step of the pipeline execution.

steps.title: Graceful error recovery in plugins
steps.description: Enhance the registry to support `RunAll(data map[string]interface{})` that executes all plugins and recovers from panics using `defer` and `recover`. Print which plugins succeeded, failed with errors, or panicked using `fmt.Printf`.
hints: Wrap each Execute call in a function with deferred recover
Use named return values for error propagation
Recover returns the panic value as interface{}

verification.failureMessage: Print success, error, and panic recovery for each plugin.
